title: A Unified Kantorovich Duality for Multimarginal Optimal Transport: the compact-case Kantorovich duality (Theorem 1)
author: Yehya Cheryala, Mokhtar Z. Alaya, Salim Bouzebda
work: A Unified Kantorovich Duality for Multimarginal Optimal Transport
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's main compact-case theorem, printed as Theorem 1 (source0.tex lines 380--389, source label KANTO), the multimarginal Kantorovich duality MOT_c(mu_1,...,mu_K) = inf_pi I(pi) = sup_{f in F_c} J(f) for compact metric spaces X_k and continuous nonnegative cost c, delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1743--1889 (147 lines; the article prints it in its appendix as one run-in block headed 'Proof of Theorem 1' and closed by the article's own Box). The proof is a full research-level duality argument rather than a citation: it identifies the dual of E = C(X_1 x ... x X_K) with the space of finite signed Radon measures through the Riesz representation theorem, computes the Legendre-Fenchel transform Theta* of the convex function Theta that encodes the constraint u >= -c, shows that the supremum defining Theta*(-pi) is attained only at nonnegative measures and that the resulting value is exactly I(pi) on plans and +infinity outside them, proves the required lower semicontinuity and the qualification condition that makes Fenchel-Rockafellar applicable, evaluates the conjugate of the sum that produces the dual problem over F_c, and finally combines the two sides and invokes the article's weak duality lemma to conclude equality. That chain (convex duality in the space of measures, qualification, and the identification of the conjugate with the optimal-transport cost) is the substance of the paper's main theorem and is far beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises. H2: a complete original research-paper main theorem with a fully written proof of moderate length whose individual steps are standard theorems applied in a non-routine sequence, not a routine verification.
